newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian lovers to hang for rat poison murder.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian lovers to hang for rat poison murder.

text.p: A Jordanian mother of nine and her lover have been sentenced to death for killing the woman's husband with rat poison, the Jordan Times reported on Wednesday.
The paper said 35-year-old Raya Musa and her 45-year-old lover Hassan Faleh decided to kill Ahmad Mireeh, 60, because they believed he would never grant his wife a divorce.
It said Raya served Mireeh, her husband for 22 years, a cocktail of sleeping pills and rat poison in their village of Der Alaa, about 25 km (15 miles) west of Amman, in January.

When sentence was passed, Raya "collapsed and then proceeded to lament, screaming she was innocent and begging for mercy," the paper said. Faleh, who bought the rat poison, was also sentenced to death.
Young teenage brides are common in Jordan although officially Jordanians are not allowed to wed until they are 16- years-old.

Tuesday's sentencing brought to 20 the number of people condemned to death in Jordan in 1996, the paper reported. It said seven executions had taken place this year. Death sentences in Jordan are usually carried out by hanging.
